planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in humus-rich, well-drained, near-neutral soil in partial shade; Galactica's Heuchera villosa parentage gives it better heat and humidity tolerance than many Heucherella cultivars.

directions: Plant in partial shade, ideally with afternoon shade, in humus-rich, well-drained soil of near-neutral pH; Galactica carries silvery, heavily dissected 5-inch leaves with deep veining and an olive-green to purple cast on new growth, topped by cream flowers in late spring. Its Heuchera villosa parentage gives it notably better tolerance of heat and humidity than many other Heucherella cultivars, making it a reasonable choice for warmer climates where some Heucherella selections struggle. It performs best and holds its color most vividly in cooler, northern growing regions, remaining evergreen through mild winters.

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in humus-rich, well-drained, near-neutral soil in partial shade; Burnished Bronze is notably hardy to zone 3, colder than most Heucherella cultivars.

directions: Plant in partial shade, ideally with afternoon shade, in humus-rich, well-drained soil of near-neutral pH; Burnished Bronze carries large, deeply divided leaves with a glossy burnished-bronze finish, topped by starry pink flowers on 18-inch scapes that may repeat bloom later in the season. It is notably cold-hardy to zone 3, a full zone or more colder than most Heucherella cultivars, making it a good choice for northern gardens wanting this genus's characteristic foliage display. Divide congested clumps every few years in spring to maintain vigor and foliage density.

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in humus-rich, well-drained, near-neutral soil in partial shade; Thunderbird's foliage color shifts dramatically from spring to summer, so expect the display to change through the season.

directions: Plant in partial shade, ideally with afternoon shade, in humus-rich, well-drained soil of near-neutral pH; Thunderbird opens in spring with bright gold foliage overlaid with brick-red pigment and gold veining, mellowing by summer to green with a retained purple center, a more dramatic seasonal color shift than many Heucherella cultivars show. Pale pinkish-white flowers open from light pink buds above the foliage. Give it consistent moisture through the growing season and divide congested clumps every few years in spring to keep the colorful foliage display dense and vigorous.

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in humus-rich, well-drained, near-neutral soil in partial shade; Gold Zebra's vivid gold-and-red foliage colors up best with some bright light rather than deep shade.

directions: Plant in partial shade, ideally with afternoon shade, in humus-rich, well-drained soil of near-neutral pH; Gold Zebra carries shocking golden-yellow leaves with a heavy smattering of bright red pigment nearly covering the leaf surface, among the most vividly patterned foliage in the genus. Small white flowers appear in late spring above the foliage mound, though the leaves remain the main attraction through the growing season. Give it bright, dappled light rather than deep shade to bring out the strongest color contrast, and divide congested clumps every few years in spring.

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in humus-rich, well-drained, near-neutral soil in partial shade; Leapfrog's Heuchera villosa parentage gives it better heat and humidity tolerance than many Heucherella cultivars.

directions: Plant in partial shade, ideally with afternoon shade, in humus-rich, well-drained soil of near-neutral pH; Leapfrog opens in spring with bright chartreuse-yellow foliage marked by a broken burgundy pattern at the leaf centers, maturing by summer to larger green leaves with dark purple centers. Ivory bottlebrush flowers appear above the foliage in late spring. Like other Heuchera villosa hybrids, it tolerates heat and humidity better than many Heucherella cultivars, making it a reasonable choice for warmer-summer gardens as well as its best performance in cooler northern climates.
